data.content_ref: inline:The target claims SRC_001 and SRC_003 are 'compatible' and 'inherit the same PIE structure,' but it explicitly names this as its substantive relation while simultaneously conceding the central mechanistic ambiguity: whether 'the ordered-pattern sum in SRC_001 (81 + 81 + 72) corresponds to a different partition of the 252 tuples than the event-sets in SRC_003 (90 + 90 + 90).' If 81+81+72 and 90+90+90 are different partitions of the same 252 tuples, then the two schemes do NOT share the same PIE structure in the mechanistically relevant sense — the pairwise-intersection sizes differ (81 vs 90), so the inclusion-exclusion terms being summed are not the same quantities. The target asserts compatibility and shared inheritance yet encodes its own refutation condition as an open question rather than verifying it. A 'relation' whose defining claim is explicitly unresolved by the artifact is not a substantive relation; it is a summary of two endpoints with a conditional hedge, which is exactly what the problem says is refuted (a summary of the endpoints is not a relation). The artifact fails to establish the dependence/compatibility it proposes because it never supplies the causal mechanism that makes 81+81+72 and 90+90+90 the same partition or proves the pairwise intersections agree — it merely flags the discrepancy and moves on.
